skill.name: parallel-agents
skill.description: Coordinate multiple AI agents on independent coding and analysis tasks without creating file or context conflicts.
skill.summary: Coordinate focused AI agents for independent coding tasks, investigations, audits, and test failures.

content.value_statement: Large coding sessions often contain independent failures that slow one agent down. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code split work safely across focused agents.
actual_capabilities: Groups unrelated failures or tasks into independent work domains.
Defines scoped agent prompts with goals, constraints, and expected deliverables.
Shows how to launch multiple Task calls in one message for parallel execution.
Explains when foreground parallel tasks are better than background tasks.
Provides integration steps for reviewing outputs, checking conflicts, and running tests.
limitations: It does not execute agents by itself or provide a runtime scheduler.
It requires the user to identify independent tasks before delegation.
It does not prevent agents from editing overlapping files unless prompts set boundaries.
It is focused on AI coding workflows, not general project management.

use_cases.title: Split independent test failures
use_cases.description: Assign separate agents to unrelated test files, then merge verified fixes after all agents report results.

use_cases.title: Parallelize focused investigations
use_cases.description: Send separate agents to inspect different subsystems when failures do not share state or ownership.

use_cases.title: Overlap audit and implementation work
use_cases.description: Run a long review in the background while another agent completes a bounded implementation task.

prompt_templates.title: Beginner task split
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when three failures are clearly unrelated.
prompt_templates.prompt: Group these failures into independent agent tasks. For each task, include scope, goal, constraints, and expected output.

prompt_templates.title: Focused test repair
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when each agent should own one test file or feature area.
prompt_templates.prompt: Create parallel Task prompts for these failing tests. Keep each prompt limited to one file area and require verification results.

prompt_templates.title: Conflict-aware delegation
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when tasks are mostly independent but file overlap is possible.
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a parallel agent plan with explicit file boundaries. Identify shared files, conflict risks, and the final integration order.

prompt_templates.title: Advanced background workflow
prompt_templates.scenario: Use when a long audit can run while implementation continues.
prompt_templates.prompt: Plan a background audit plus foreground implementation workflow. Include when to collect results, how to reconcile findings, and what tests to run.

output_examples.input: Three unrelated test suites fail in authentication, API routing, and UI components.
output_examples.output: A three-agent delegation plan with separate scopes, constraints, expected deliverables, and a final integration checklist.

output_examples.input: A security review is long-running, but a login form change is ready to build.
output_examples.output: A background review plan paired with a foreground implementation task and a result collection step before final response.

output_examples.input: Several agents may need the same shared configuration file.
output_examples.output: A conflict-aware task split that isolates investigation work and reserves shared-file edits for the integration phase.

best_practices: Use parallel agents only when tasks have separate causes, files, or subsystems.
Give every agent exact scope, constraints, success criteria, and expected output.
Review all outputs, check for conflicts, and run the full test suite before merging.
anti_patterns: Do not send vague prompts such as fixing all tests without file boundaries.
Do not assign agents to modify the same files at the same time.
Do not leave background task results uncollected before ending the response.

faq.question: When should I use this skill?
faq.answer: Use it when you have three or more independent coding tasks or failures that can be investigated separately.

faq.question: Does it run agents automatically?
faq.answer: No. It provides guidance and prompt patterns for using Task and TaskOutput tools in supported environments.

faq.question: Can it help with failing tests?
faq.answer: Yes. It is especially useful when failures belong to different files, services, or UI areas.

faq.question: How does it reduce conflicts?
faq.answer: It asks you to define file scope, constraints, and output requirements before dispatching agents.

faq.question: When should I avoid it?
faq.answer: Avoid it when tasks share state, require the same files, or have one connected root cause.

faq.question: Does it support Codex and Claude Code?
faq.answer: Yes. The report marks compatibility with Claude, Codex, and Claude Code workflows.
